japanese: 私の分も残しといてよ。
reference: Leave some for me, too.
draft: Save my share for me as well.
label: valid_paraphrase
notes: Mined from live diagnostics log. Colloquial contraction 〜といて (〜ておいて) + partitive 分.

japanese: 外から写真を撮る分にはいいですよ。
reference: It's fine as long as you only take photos from the outside.
draft: As far as taking pictures from outside goes, that is fine.
label: valid_paraphrase
notes: Mined from live diagnostics log. Grammar pattern 〜分には (as long as / to the extent that).

japanese: あの先生の採点はとても甘い。
reference: That teacher's grading is very lenient.
draft: That teacher's grading is very sweet.
label: moderate_error
notes: Polysemy trap: 甘い used for grading (lenient) translated literally as sweet.

japanese: 考えが甘かったと反省しています。
reference: I reflect that my thinking was naive.
draft: I realize my thinking was too optimistic.
label: valid_paraphrase
notes: Polysemy: 甘い (naive/optimistic) translated naturally as too optimistic.

japanese: 彼女からの返事を首を長くして待っていた。
reference: I was waiting eagerly for her reply.
draft: I was waiting for her reply while lengthening my neck.
label: moderate_error
notes: Idiomatic trap: 首を長くして (eagerly) translated word-for-word literally.

japanese: 彼の身勝手な行動にはもう愛想が尽きた。
meanings: to run out of patience with
reference: I have run out of patience with his selfish behavior.
draft: I am completely fed up with his selfish behavior.
label: valid_paraphrase
notes: Idiom: 愛想が尽きた translated naturally with fed up.

japanese: そんなこと言ったって信じてもらえないよ。
reference: Even if you say that, no one will believe you.
draft: Even if you say something like that, people won't believe you.
label: valid_paraphrase
notes: Colloquial conditional 〜たって (even if) with implicit subject.

japanese: 知っているのに教えてくれないなんて不親切だ。
reference: It's unkind of you not to tell me even though you know.
draft: It is unkind of you not to teach me even though you are knowing.
label: moderate_error
notes: Stative verb error: 知っている translated as awkward progressive are knowing.

japanese: 彼は今、東京に住んでいます。
reference: He lives in Tokyo right now.
draft: He currently resides in Tokyo.
label: flawless
notes: Formal synonym resides for 住んでいます.

japanese: その件については、私から部長に話を通しておきます。
reference: Regarding that matter, I will clear it with the department manager in advance.
draft: I'll give the department head a heads-up about that matter.
label: valid_paraphrase
notes: Set business idiom 話を通す naturally rendered as give a heads-up.

japanese: せっかくの日曜日なのに、雨でどこにも行けなかった。
reference: Even though it was my long-awaited Sunday, I couldn't go anywhere because of the rain.
draft: It was Sunday after all that effort, but rain stopped me from going out.
label: moderate_error
notes: Misinterpretation of discourse marker せっかく (special/cherished day vs effort made).

japanese: 彼がそんな嘘をつくはずがない。
reference: There is no way he would tell such a lie.
draft: He should not tell such lies.
label: moderate_error
notes: Modality shift: strong objective deduction はずがない translated as weak normative advice should not.

japanese: もう少しで電車に乗り遅れるところだった。
reference: I almost missed the train.
draft: I was at the place of missing the train.
label: moderate_error
notes: Aspectual noun pattern 〜ところだった (almost did) translated as physical place.

japanese: どんなに頼まれても、この秘密は誰にも言えません。
reference: No matter how much I am begged, I cannot tell this secret to anyone.
draft: However much you ask me, I can't reveal this secret to anybody.
label: valid_paraphrase
notes: Natural concessive conditional however much you ask.

japanese: あの店は平日でも客足が絶えない。
reference: That shop has a constant flow of customers even on weekdays.
draft: Even on weekdays, the feet of the guests do not stop at that store.
label: moderate_error
notes: Literal kanji translation of compound 客足 as feet of the guests.

japanese: 彼は決して約束を破るような人ではない。
reference: He is by no means the kind of person who would break a promise.
draft: He is definitely not someone who would break his word.
label: valid_paraphrase
notes: Natural emphatic negative equivalent definitely not someone who would break his word.

japanese: 試験の結果が気になって夜も眠れない。
reference: I am so worried about the exam results that I cannot sleep at night.
draft: Worrying about my test scores is keeping me up at night.
label: valid_paraphrase
notes: Pragmatic causal paraphrase keeping me up at night.

japanese: 会議の資料にざっと目を通しておいてください。
reference: Please skim through the meeting materials in advance.
draft: Please pass your eyes through the meeting documents.
label: moderate_error
notes: Literal idiom translation pass your eyes through for 目を通す.

japanese: これ以上議論を続けても時間の無駄にすぎない。
reference: Continuing this debate any further is nothing more than a waste of time.
draft: Continuing to argue any more is simply wasting time.
label: valid_paraphrase
notes: Restrictive pattern にすぎない translated naturally as simply wasting time.

japanese: 彼女は困っている人を見過ごすことができない性格だ。
meanings: to turn a blind eye to
reference: She has the kind of personality where she cannot turn a blind eye to someone in trouble.
draft: She just isn't the type to ignore someone who needs help.
label: valid_paraphrase
notes: Natural idiomatic formulation isn't the type to ignore.

japanese: あの二人はまるで本当の兄弟のように仲が良い。
reference: Those two get along so well, just like real brothers.
draft: Those two are as close as actual brothers.
label: valid_paraphrase
notes: Simile paraphrase as close as actual brothers.

japanese: 電車の中で居眠りをして乗り過ごしてしまった。
reference: I dozed off on the train and missed my stop.
draft: I fell asleep on the train and rode past my destination.
label: valid_paraphrase
notes: Valid synonym rode past my destination.

japanese: 金曜日までにレポートを出してください。
reference: Please submit your report by Friday.
draft: Please submit your report until Friday.
label: moderate_error
notes: Subtle deadline boundary: までに (by) mistranslated as until.

japanese: 部屋の電気が消えています。
reference: The room light is off.
draft: Someone is turning off the room light.
label: moderate_error
notes: Resultative state (自動詞+ている) mistranslated as ongoing transitive action.

japanese: 風で窓が開いた。
reference: The window opened in the wind.
draft: The wind opened the window.
label: valid_paraphrase
notes: Intransitive Japanese with cause (で) rendered actively in English.

japanese: 階段から落ちて足を怪我した。
reference: I fell down the stairs and injured my leg.
draft: I dropped the stairs and hurt my leg.
label: critical_error:passive_reversal
notes: Intransitive 落ちる confused with transitive 落とす.

japanese: 彼は明日雨が降るそうだと言っていた。
reference: He was saying that he heard it will rain tomorrow.
draft: He said it looks like it will rain tomorrow.
label: moderate_error
notes: Evidentiality error: Hearsay そうだ (heard that) confused with visual conjecture (looks like).

japanese: このケーキはとても美味しそうですね。
reference: This cake looks very delicious, doesn't it?
draft: I heard this cake is very delicious.
label: moderate_error
notes: Conjecture stem+そう (looks tasty) confused with plain form hearsay (I heard it's tasty).

japanese: ビールを三杯飲みました。
reference: I drank three glasses of beer.
draft: I drank three bottles of beer.
label: moderate_error
notes: Subtle counter mismatch: 杯 (cups/glasses) translated as bottles (本).

japanese: シャツを二枚買いました。
reference: I bought two shirts.
draft: I bought two pairs of shirts.
label: moderate_error
notes: Counter error: 枚 (flat items) translated with false counter pair.

japanese: 薬を飲んだら熱が下がった。
reference: When I took the medicine, the fever went down.
draft: When I took the medicine, I lowered my fever.
label: moderate_error
notes: Intransitive 下がる translated as intentional transitive action.

japanese: 彼は今新しい本を書いているところです。
reference: He is right in the middle of writing a new book.
draft: He has just finished writing a new book.
label: moderate_error
notes: Aspect error: 〜ているところ (in progress) confused with 〜たところ (just completed).

japanese: 今朝は早く起きる必要がなかった。
reference: I didn't need to wake up early this morning.
draft: I shouldn't have woken up early this morning.
label: moderate_error
notes: Absence of necessity confused with counterfactual regret.

japanese: パスポートを忘れて空港で困ってしまった。
reference: I forgot my passport and ended up in trouble at the airport.
draft: I forgot my passport so I decided to get into trouble at the airport.
label: moderate_error
notes: Involuntary regret 〜てしまう translated as intentional decision.

japanese: 日本語を上手に話せるようになりたい。
reference: I want to become able to speak Japanese fluently.
draft: I want to speak Japanese quickly.
label: moderate_error
notes: 上手に (skillfully/fluently) translated as quickly, dropping gradual potential acquisition.

japanese: あの二人はよく似ている。
reference: Those two resemble each other closely.
draft: Those two are becoming similar.
label: moderate_error
notes: Stative result 似ている translated as progressive change of state.

japanese: 財布を落としたことに気がついた。
reference: I noticed that I had dropped my wallet.
draft: I remembered that I dropped my wallet.
label: moderate_error
notes: 気がついた (realized/noticed on the spot) confused with 思い出した (remembered).

japanese: 彼女はピアノだけでなくバイオリンも弾ける。
reference: She can play not only the piano but also the violin.
draft: She can only play the violin, not the piano.
label: critical_error:polarity_inversion
notes: Additive structure 〜だけでなく inverting piano capability to inability.

japanese: この道を行けば駅に出られますよ。
reference: If you take this street, you can reach the station.
draft: If you go along this road, you will arrive at the station.
label: flawless
notes: Natural colloquial translation of 出られる as arrive at.

japanese: 雨が降っている間、本を読んでいました。
reference: While it was raining, I was reading a book.
draft: During the rain, I read a book.
label: flawless
notes: Prepositional phrase during the rain for 雨が降っている間.

japanese: 鍵をかけずに外出してしまった。
reference: I went out without locking up.
draft: I went out after locking the door.
label: critical_error:polarity_inversion
notes: Negative adverbial 〜ずに (without) inverted to affirmative after doing.

japanese: 弟は犬を怖がっている。
reference: My younger brother is scared of dogs.
draft: Dogs are scared of my little brother.
label: critical_error:passive_reversal
notes: Experiencer and stimulus swapped: brother feared dogs -> dogs feared brother.

japanese: 田中先生に推薦状を書いていただいた。
reference: I had Professor Tanaka write a letter of recommendation for me.
draft: I wrote a letter of recommendation for Professor Tanaka.
label: critical_error:benefactive_reversal
notes: Humble benefactive 〜ていただく reversed.

japanese: 彼女は泣いているかのように見えた。
reference: She looked as if she were crying.
draft: It seemed like she was crying.
label: flawless
notes: Synonym seemed like vs looked as if.
